column1: # *** LEANDRO LERENA AND LUCIA LLANOS - A PUBLISHED NULL, BROKEN BY A RECORD THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD.
# On 10 October this archive published a model controlled null: Leandro Lorena and his wife Llanos
# appear in ONE record on earth, the army card of their son Salvador. The search was signed in, the
# constraint bound, eleven Llanos rows came back across five countries, and exactly one was theirs.
# *** THE SEARCH WAS SOUND AND THE CONCLUSION WAS WRONG, because a spouse-pair query is structurally
# blind to a census - and the census rows were already in this register under a different spelling. ***
*** THE NULL THAT WAS TRUE OF THE QUERY, NOT OF THE INDEX ***
column2: 1895 Argentine National Census, Seccion 18 Subdivision 34, Ciudad de Buenos Aires - image ark 3:1:S3HT-XX67-Q4K, apid TH-266-13033-138829-16, read at the plate
column3: *** THE LEANDRO LORENA / LLANOS HOUSEHOLD, WHICH THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED AS A TRUE NULL ***
column4: On 10 October 2026, signed in and properly controlled, the query q.surname=Lorena with q.spouseSurname=Llanos bound correctly, returned eleven LLANOS rows across five countries, and matched this couple *** exactly once - on the army card itself. *** It was written up as the model of what a controlled null looks like, and published on open question 1: *** 'the army card is their only record in the index, in any country.' ***
column5: *** THEY ARE IN THE 1895 CENSUS, AND THIS ARCHIVE HAS HELD THE ROWS SINCE BEFORE THE NULL WAS WRITTEN. *** Lines 7 to 11 of the sheet: *** LERENA Leandro, varon, 38, casado, Espanol, born SEGOVIA ***; *** LLANOS Lucia, mujer, 32, casada ***; *** LERENA Emilia, 9, born in Spain ***; *** LERENA Francisco, 5, born LA PLATA ***; and *** Paulina, 8 MESES, portena. ***

column1: *** WHY THE NULL HELD, AND IT IS A METHOD FINDING ***
column3: *** A SPOUSE-PAIR QUERY CANNOT SEE A CENSUS ***
column4: The 10 October search was q.surname + q.spouseSurname. It is the right tool for parish and civil registers, where a marriage is recorded as a relationship between two people.
column5: *** A CENSUS DOES NOT RECORD MARRIAGE AS A RELATIONSHIP. *** It records a list of people in a dwelling, each indexed as a separate persona with no spouse edge at all - so a spouse-constrained query is structurally blind to it no matter how well it binds. *** And the surname differs: the card says LORENA, the census says LERENA. *** The null was true of the query shape and false of the index, which is the one disguise data/false-zeros.tsv did not yet carry.

column1: *** AND THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THE ANSWER ***
column3: *** Leandro LERENA b.1857 Spain, Emilia b.1886, Francisco b.1890, Paulina b.1895 - all four already in this register, all four marked 'Leandro's household' ***
column4: Nothing connected them to the army card. The register said *** 'Head of a SEPARATE, Spanish-born family' *** while open question 1 said the same man was a true null.
column5: *** TWO STATEMENTS ABOUT ONE HOUSEHOLD, BOTH PUBLISHED, NEITHER LOOKING AT THE OTHER. *** The missing link was the wife: *** LUCIA LLANOS was never entered ***, and she is the only name the two records share. *** An archive does not need a new record to make this mistake; it needs two rows that never meet. ***

column1: *** WHAT THE PLATE ADDS BEYOND THE IDENTIFICATION ***
column2: the same sheet, columns F and H
column4: The register had only 'Spain' for Leandro and nothing for his work.
column5: *** Leandro Lerena was born at SEGOVIA *** - a Spanish origin this archive has not met, and not Navarrete. He is *** literate *** (the sheet's 'sabe leer' column reads si for him and for Lucia) and his occupation reads *** 'F.te de Aceite' - an oil maker or oil dealer. *** The children date the emigration: *** Emilia born in Spain about 1886, Francisco born at LA PLATA about 1890 ***, so they crossed between those years. Paulina was eight months old when the census was taken.

column1: *** SALVADOR, AND WHY THE FIT IS GOOD ***
column2: the army card of Cajon 985, order 666, against the census sheet
column3: *** SALVADOR LORENA, born 1896 - the year after this census ***
column4: The card names him as the son of Leandro Lorena and Lucio [Lucia] Llanos.
column5: *** The household on the sheet is complete to an eight-month-old in 1895, and Salvador arrives in 1896. *** He is the next child, and he is not on the sheet because he had not been born. *** NOT PROVED BY A SINGLE ACT, AND SAID SO: *** the identification rests on a distinctive surname pair (Leandro with a Llanos), one city, a documented Lerena/Lorena spelling pair, and a birth year that fits the gap exactly. *** What would settle it: Salvador's 1896 birth registration, which would name both parents. ***
